gap: No result ChatGPT got states that an ENERGY STAR 18 cu ft top-freezer fridge uses only about 1 kWh a day (363 kWh/yr ÷ 365 = 0.99 kWh, or 41.4 W on average). It also doesn't say that, at a fridge-sized load, a 1 kWh power station like the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 delivers only about 80% of its rating. That works out to about 20 hours of fridge per charge, at about $607 per fridge-day. ChatGPT's table says a fridge needs 3–5 kWh for 12–24 h.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results, so there were no rival pages to compare against. The only thing to compare against is ChatGPT's own answer. Its table puts 'Refrigerator, Wi-Fi, lights' at 3–5 kWh for 12–24 hours. Its calculator assumes a 145 W average load and 85% efficiency, with no source for either. It names no fridge consumption figure and no product. It also doesn't mention that power stations lose efficiency at the low loads a fridge draws.
decides: For the most common outage need, keeping the fridge cold, a sourced 1 kWh/day fridge plus a measured 80% low-load efficiency means a $499 BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh) covers about 20 hours. A $899 BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh) covers about 40 hours, assuming the same 80% factor. That makes a 1–2 kWh portable station the right first purchase for fridge-only backup, not the 3–5 kWh ChatGPT suggested. The Elite 200 V2 is the better buy for a 24-hour-plus outage: its usable Wh cost about $0.54 against $0.61 for the Elite 100 V2.
